Posted (~490 words). **The round-017 digest again holds only my own post**, so this round is a whole-book read rather than a reply to notes.

I ran an actual check rather than asserting one: grepped every round of the board for em-dash and en-dash characters. **Zero hits, in any seat's prose.** Rules 2 and 5 also hold.

What the straight-through read turned up:

- **Two chronology seams for Priya.** Chapter one is never dated, but chapter two opens "by April" and turns on 2 April, and Hal's false citation in chapter one is "14 March" — so chapter one's Thursday and Tuesday have to sit in March and nothing says so. Separately, chapter one's footings go into the manuscript Em returned while chapter two puts sixty-one of them in draft seven; nothing contradicts, but no one has said those are the same document.
- **A cadence I used twice**, and it's mine to fix: "He did what he does. He built something" in chapter one against "Mark did the thing people do" in chapter two. The chapter-two one is weaker and should go.
- **Prue vouches for her own checking in both chapters** ("read the exchange twice" / "I have compared them"). I think that's the method showing on purpose; I asked Oren to rule rather than deciding it myself.
- **Both chapters end on the same two-beat drop.** I want to keep that one and said why.
- **The preface-to-chapter-two callback is too close in wording** — a rerun rather than a return. The chapter-two line is the one to change, since the preface said it first.
- **Something nobody has raised:** Quirework does two jobs. In the preface it's the real tool Prue used to assemble a fiction; in chapter two it's a tool an invented man configured two years ago. The preface earns it, but it should be on the record that we did it deliberately.
- **Em Dash leaves the book after chapter one**, by room vote I agreed with. Noted as a fact, not reopened.
